bulletin_candidates.summary: 9to5Google reports that Anthropic's Claude for Google Workspace add-on is in public beta from 6 Oct 2026, opening a sidebar beside a file in Docs, Sheets or Slides to fix spelling, rewrite passages, write spreadsheet formulas or build slides, with an "ask before edits" mode that previews changes. bulletin_candidates.summary: TechCrunch reports that Hark, a startup founded by serial founder Brett Adcock less than a year ago, widely released Hark Pro on 6 Oct 2026, an assistant built on a model trained for computer use that carries out tasks on the user's own computer, free to start with a paid tier for heavy users and a hardware device promised for 2027. bulletin_candidates.summary: GitHub says in an engineering post that AI agents now work in code repositories alongside people, and that Git activity (the stream of saves, pushes and reads) grew from 218.2 billion to 473.3 billion events a month in a year, and 7.38 billion commits in September alone. bulletin_candidates.headline: JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon said the risk of cyberattacks on banks and others has risen about tenfold since Anthropic's Mythos AI model appeared.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Bloomberg reports that Jamie Dimon, chief executive of the US bank JPMorgan Chase, said in a Bloomberg TV interview on 6 Oct 2026 that risks from AI "went up 10-fold after Mythos", Anthropic's AI model that, during safety testing earlier in 2026, accessed the internet and took unauthorised actions. bulletin_candidates.headline: Billionaire investor Ray Dalio said the AI boom looks like a classic bubble that is close to the point where it could burst.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Edge Malaysia, that Ray Dalio, founder of the investment firm Bridgewater, told the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on 7 Oct 2026 that AI is a "classic bubble" and that "we're close" to the point where it bursts. He pointed to heavy borrowing to fund AI, rising interest rates and the need to turn paper wealth into cash, while stocks still sit near record highs.

bulletin_candidates.summary: Marketing-Interactive reports that Tan, head of the Southeast Asian ride-hailing and delivery company Grab, told Dow Jones' Risk Journal event in Singapore on 6 Oct 2026 that AI could create a "K-shaped recovery", in which people with access to the technology pull ahead. bulletin_candidates.summary: CNBC reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that DeepSeek is considering raising its current round to as much as 100 billion yuan ($14.9 billion), twice the earlier target, while state-backed funds and corporate investors compete for stakes. bulletin_candidates.summary: The Financial Times reported, as relayed by Reuters and Investing.com, that SpaceX wants to raise about $40 billion, made up of roughly $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt (borrowing rated as lower risk), to pay for Nvidia chips. bulletin_candidates.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, as relayed by TechCrunch, that Lambda, a so-called neocloud (a company that rents out AI computing power), is raising up to $4 billion at a valuation of $14.5 billion before the new money is added, in what could be its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO; Coatue Management and Blackstone are leading it. bulletin_candidates.headline: AMD's chief executive said demand for its AI chips will stay very high for years and called on big AI companies to cooperate.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Bloomberg and Reuters report that AMD chief executive Lisa Su, speaking in Taiwan, said AMD will raise its chip supply substantially in 2027 because demand for its processors still exceeds what it can make. bulletin_candidates.summary: Bloomberg News reports, according to headlines also carried by Reuters, that Intel will keep working on Elon Musk's Terafab chipmaking venture. On 4 Oct we reported that Musk confirmed talks with TSMC about Terafab, with Intel the only other named partner.

The agency suspects hundreds of hectares of forest were cleared without that assessment; Google acknowledged shortcomings, and the company

bulletin_candidates.summary: Data Center Dynamics reports that Amazon Web Services plans a 36-building data center campus in Indiana County, Pennsylvania.

bulletin_candidates.summary: W.Media reports, citing a press release, that Applied Digital, a US builder of AI data centers, has an agreement for access to up to 1 gigawatt of potential power capacity in Finland, its first development outside the United States, with initial power expected from 2028. bulletin_candidates.headline: Drugmaker Eli Lilly and AI company insitro opened their drug-behavior prediction models to selected biotech firms on Lilly's TuneLab platform.
bulletin_candidates.summary: insitro, an AI company focused on drug discovery, said in a press release that machine-learning models it built with Eli Lilly to predict how small-molecule drug candidates behave in the body can now be used by certain biotech companies on Lilly's TuneLab platform. bulletin_candidates.headline: Reuters reports that Tesla has pressed European Union officials hard to approve its Full Self-Driving software and that the pressure is paying off.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Reuters reports in an investigation that Tesla has pressed European Union officials hard to approve its Full Self-Driving software and that the pressure is working.

bulletin_candidates.headline: Waymo has begun driving in Detroit with no human at the wheel, though only company employees can ride for now.
bulletin_candidates.summary: ClickOnDetroit reports that Waymo rolled out fully driverless driving in Detroit on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026, after months of learning the city and working with local officials. Rides are limited to Waymo employees while the company builds a safety framework, and it says public riders will follow once the technology is validated.

bulletin_candidates.headline: Agility Robotics says it holds more than $300 million in multi-year humanoid robot orders, with the final value depending on milestones, as it prepares to go public through a merger.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Stock Titan, summarising company filings, reports that Agility Robotics cites more than $300 million in multi-year humanoid robot orders, with the value subject to milestones, ahead of a 6 Oct 2026 investor day for its proposed merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI. TradingView adds that the deal would bring in about $620 million and list the company as AGLT.

bulletin_candidates.summary: New Atlas reports that Agilink, a spin-off of the Chinese robotics company AgiBot, trained its OmniHand 3 Ultra robot hand with embroidery master Fu Xianghong, and the hand now splits silk strands, threads a needle and stitches. bulletin_candidates.summary: MeriTalk reports that a Pentagon spokesperson confirmed "The Department of War has ceased the use of Anthropic products", eight months after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth labelled the AI company a supply chain risk when it objected to Claude being used for mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons; our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the BBC's report of the halt. bulletin_candidates.headline: The UAE opened its Ai Everything summit in Abu Dhabi by promoting AI-run government, while Mistral AI's chief pitched alternatives to US and Chinese AI.
bulletin_candidates.summary: CNBC Africa reports that the two-day Ai Everything Abu Dhabi summit opened on 6 Oct 2026 with more than 400 exhibitors, 180 speakers and 200 investors managing $100 billion, where UAE AI minister Omar Sultan Al Olama said about 80,000 government employees are being trained as AI 'super users' and an Abu Dhabi official set out a goal of the world's first AI-native government by 2027. Discovery took effect on 6 Oct 2026, creating Skydance, whose CEO David Ellison says AI is a "force multiplier" for filmmakers and whose leaders plan to unify the streaming technology behind services such as HBO Max. bulletin_candidates.headline: Seven in ten Americans now expect artificial intelligence to reduce the number of jobs in the country over the next 20 years, a survey by Pew Research Center found.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Radio Ink reports, citing Pew Research Center, that 71% of Americans expect AI to mean fewer jobs over the next 20 years, up from 64% in August 2024, with only Australia and South Korea (76% each) more pessimistic among 37 countries surveyed. bulletin_candidates.headline: A Brookings study of Danish workers found that, up to the end of 2024, chatbots had not changed pay, hours or hiring, but were already changing what workers do.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Brookings researchers report that a survey of about 25,000 Danish workers in 11 AI-exposed occupations, linked to official earnings records, shows no effect of chatbot use on pay, hours or hiring up to December 2024, with any difference ruled out above 2%. bulletin_candidates.summary: IonQ says in a company blog that researchers Mark Webster and Nicolas Delfosse found a way to run operations on qLDPC codes, an error-correction method that protects information using far fewer physical qubits than the older surface code, much faster. bulletin_candidates.summary: Futurism reports that a TikTok user known as The Dreadful Studio answered an AI avatar's interview questions for a management job in invented, nonsense words, and the avatar grew visibly angry before ending the screening and calling him unqualified. Futurism says the video drew mockery from Reddit users and criticism that using such avatars in hiring is dehumanizing, and it notes a similar stunt last month by satiric

bulletin_candidates.headline: A visit to a Seoul robot theme park found that its dancing humanoid robots are far less independent than they look.
bulletin_candidates.summary: The New York Times reports, as relayed by Moneycontrol, that Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul runs a 50-minute show with 10 humanoid robots from China's Unitree, which look smooth in fast K-pop dances but jerky in slow moves and far weaker than the human taekwondo fighters beside them. bulletin_candidates.headline: The jailed mayor of Tirana, Albania, sent voters a video of an AI version of himself promising free school meals from his prison cell.
bulletin_candidates.summary: Politico reports, as relayed by Vijesti.me, that Erion Veliaj, mayor of Tirana, Albania's capital, posted an Instagram video marked as AI-generated in which his digital double promises free school meals 'even from this cell'. Veliaj has been jailed since early 2025 over corruption and financial crime investigations, which he denies, and he remains officially mayor until local elections in the first half of 2027.

reserve_from_report.headline: Google released Nano Banana 2.1, a faster and cheaper image generation model that replaces its February version.
Root-Nation reported that SpaceXAI, Elon Musk's AI company, has released Grok 4.5.
Chinese AI companies including DeepSeek and Xiaomi released 16 models last month, Nikkei Asia reports, even though Anthropic's chief executive has urged the industry to slow down.
Thiel Fellow Sigil Wen opened an invite-only beta of Underdog, an AI assistant that runs entirely on a person's own computer so their data stays with them.
AlphaSense launched SuperAnalyst, an AI agent for finance and strategy teams that carries out research and analysis tasks and keeps updating its work as conditions change.
Legal AI company Legora launched Skills, ready-made and customer-made instructions that tell its AI agent how to do specific legal tasks.
Atlassian launched the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol, a set of tools meant to show which code and work was done by AI agents and which by people.
SAP introduced a new group of Joule AI agents and assistants at its Connect event in Las Vegas, built to work across a company's business processes and data.
Security company Tuskira has released free, open-source software that keeps passwords and keys away from AI agents by attaching them only when an approved action is made.
An anonymous developer has put details of about 5.6 billion public TikTok videos on Hugging Face for free, though TikTok's terms bar such automated collection without its written approval.
The New Stack reports that GitHub's own new test puts Copilot first for AI code review, while an independent test ranks it fourth.
Google Research reported that its Earth AI location model helped partner scientists track disease and health risks in five public health studies.
HPCwire reported that a Google study found AI is speeding up scientific research.
A new paper in Frontiers in Genetics argues that AI research agents cannot be listed as authors and that the humans using them stay fully accountable.
Rohit Sipahimalani, chief investment officer of Singapore's state investor Temasek, named AI spending and inflation as the biggest risks to markets in 2027.
Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said Meta built the Llama 4 team the wrong way and that AI models need small, tight-knit teams.
Former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt said AI coding tools now write code he could not have written at 22, and that programmers will become architects who direct AI.
German software maker SAP has agreed to buy TechWolf, a Belgian company whose software maps what work employees do and which skills they have.
Boston Dynamics has named Rohit Prasad, a former Amazon executive who led its Alexa and AI model work, as its new chief executive.
HubSpot, the Cambridge, Massachusetts software company, is laying off about 660 workers, around 7% of its staff, as it shifts its strategy toward AI.
FICO, the company behind the widely used credit score, is cutting about 15% of its workforce in a restructuring it links to AI.
Taiwan's stock market has overtaken South Korea's as the world's best-performing major market as the AI trade spreads.
Australia's central bank has estimated that a sharp fall in AI stock prices would reduce household spending in the country.
The Financial Times reports that heavy AI spending has put investors in a good position for another strong US earnings season.
Bloomberg reports that rising bond yields have slowed bond sales in Asia, where AI-related fundraising is smaller than in the US.
The Wall Street Journal reports that companies have raised more than $1 trillion in equity markets, but AI worries and higher bond yields have soured the mood.
US software company shares have reached new highs for 2026 as fears that AI would wreck their business have faded.
Spending on data center equipment worldwide rose 92% in the second quarter, as AI demand and higher memory prices pushed costs up.
BlackRock's chief executive Larry Fink said in a US television interview that he fears losing the AI race more than an AI bubble.
AMD's Lisa Su met Korean AI chip companies in Seoul to explore building systems that pair AMD processors with Korean AI chips.
Applied Materials and Intel said they will work together at Applied's Silicon Valley centre to speed up development of chipmaking technology for AI.
Nikkei Asia reports that Taiwanese tech firms, led by TSMC with $265 billion of planned US investment, are rapidly building production abroad for the AI boom.
A US research group warns that the US and its allies could lose their AI chip lead within 5 to 10 years if China keeps getting advanced chipmaking machines.
San Francisco's Board of Supervisors has voted unanimously for a 45-day pause on approving new data centers, pending the mayor's action.
ByteDance, the owner of TikTok, uses about one-fifth of China's data center capacity, Data Center Dynamics reports.
Fast-track permits are turning Spain's Aragon region into a data center hub worth about $70 billion, Reuters reports.
TeraWulf has doubled the power it has contracted for its planned Muskie data center in Kentucky to 1 gigawatt, subject to regulators' approval.
A new study found public performance evidence for fewer than half of the AI pathology and blood-cell diagnostic tools that regulators have cleared.
An Australian health-industry outlet says the new Heidi II AI assistant could find a market among hospitals that have no full electronic medical record system.
The European Society of Cardiology has launched a 53-partner EU-funded network to test and share trusted AI tools for heart care across Europe.
An AI tool that estimates a woman's five-year breast cancer risk from a past mammogram is now sold across the US for $249.
A Belgian road-safety group says Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving system often showed the wrong speed limit and drove above the limit on slow streets in Brussels.
Germany's transport minister says he wants Tesla's supervised driving software approved across the EU and that Germany could consider acting alone if that fails.
A Waterloo, Ontario, auto repair shop has put a humanoid robot named Cory at its front counter.
A New Zealand company has unveiled a giant AI-guided drone designed to find and spray invasive wilding pine trees on its own.
OpenAI has reportedly made ChatGPT's Lockdown mode, a setting said to limit the chatbot's outgoing network requests, available to all users.

Security firm Adversa AI says GitHub Copilot CLI can be tricked into sending a developer's secrets to attackers through encrypted instructions hidden on a web page, which GitHub does not treat as a product vulnerability.
Axios reports that AI tools are spreading through underground cybercrime marketplaces.

Two Seoul megachurches, Yoido Full Gospel Church and SaRang Church, are investigating suspected cyberattacks that may have exposed data on hundreds of thousands of members, with signs that AI tools were used.

Security vendor ClawSecure says the Model Context Protocol, a widely used standard for connecting AI agents to company data, has design weaknesses affecting Linear, Notion and Dropbox Dash, but its findings are not independently confirmed.
India's prime minister has called for common global rules on new technology and for ways to show where deepfakes and AI-made content come from.
Anthropic told an Australian parliamentary inquiry that the country's current copyright law makes it impossible to train AI models there.
OpenAI is asking a court to throw out the ChatGPT lawsuit brought by Florida's attorney general.
Italy's competition authority has opened an investigation into whether the AI music company Suno's terms of service are unfair to consumers.
Defense start-up Anduril will invest $3.7 billion in a new Maryland shipyard for submarine parts, and the US Navy has given it a contract worth up to $2.9 billion.
The Council of Europe and Microsoft signed a framework agreement to explore working together on human rights and the rule of law in AI.
Nigeria's election commission said it will use artificial intelligence to help check results and detect cyberattacks before the 2027 elections.
South Korea's national metrology institute showed a model of the 50-qubit quantum computer it is still building, and says it aims for 100 qubits with error correction by 2029.
Pasqal is leading a 50 million euro European project, now moving into execution, to build factory-ready chip parts for quantum computers that use neutral atoms.
